stories.title: A calculation model for the loess collapse coefficient considering progressive wetting dry density and applied vertical pressure
stories.description: Predicting wetting-induced collapse of loess requires accounting for the coupled effects of applied pressure, moisture state, and pore structure. Laboratory collapse tests were conducted on remolded Ili loess at different water contents, dry densities, and applied vertical pressures. A three-factor coupled model was developed using dimensionless pressure, degree of saturation, and void ratio. The main contribution is a continuous parameterization that allows the collapse coefficient to be calculated across the investigated soil states without independently refitting each water-content–dry-density combination. The model describes the nonlinear pressure-dependent response and incorporates moisture and pore-structure effects through saturation- and void-ratio-dependent parameters. Evaluation against the laboratory data yielded an overall coefficient of determination of R2 = 0.783. A dimensionless wetting parameter was introduced to evaluate changes in remaining collapse potential across independently prepared moisture states within the tested range. An engineering-scale application to a 30 m loess profile predicted a self-weight collapse settlement of 3330.71 mm, compared with a reported field measurement of 3520 mm, corresponding to a relative error of 5.38%. Because some field conditions exceeded the laboratory calibration range, this comparison indicates application potential rather than general validation. The proposed formulation links routinely measured soil properties with collapse-coefficient estimation and layerwise settlement assessment.

stories.title: Integrated bioinformatic analysis identifies distinct neddylation-associated proteasome genes and immune-related features in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma
stories.description: Neddylation contributes to cancer progression, but its relationship with proteasome-related genes and the immune microenvironment in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) remains unclear. We aimed to identify neddylation-associated genes in LSCC and characterize their molecular, metabolic, and immune features. Transcriptomic data from The Cancer Genome Atlas and Gene Expression Omnibus were analyzed using differential expression, functional enrichment, and machine-learning approaches. Key genes were further evaluated by survival, pathway, immune infiltration, and somatic mutation analyses and validated by quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) in five paired LSCC and adjacent tissues. Seventy-four differentially expressed neddylation-related genes were identified. Four genes, KCTD6, PSMB2, PSMB4, and PSMD2, were selected by both LASSO and SVM-RFE. KCTD6-associated genes were enriched in bile acid metabolism, while macrophage M0 and resting CD4 + memory T cells were associated with prognosis. Lower PSMB4 and PSMD2 expression was associated with immune escape-related features. qRT-PCR in five paired specimens confirmed the predicted direction of expression change for all four genes (KCTD6 lower, and PSMB2, PSMB4, and PSMD2 higher in tumor); given the small paired sample, this provides directional confirmation only and does not establish biomarker performance. We identified a distinct set of proteasome-related neddylation-associated genes associated with metabolic and immune characteristics in LSCC. These findings suggest potential links between neddylation-associated proteasome genes and the immune microenvironment in LSCC.

stories.title: Deployment of edge-lightweight AI vertical models in multimodal anomaly detection and energy optimization of tech-long production line
stories.description: Aiming at the problems that the abnormal state of high-speed liquid packaging production lines is difficult to identify in time, the computing power of edge controller is limited, and the energy consumption regulation and condition monitoring are separated from each other, a multimodal lightweight artificial intelligence (AI) system embedded in Tech-Long production controller is constructed; this realizes the collaborative optimization of abnormal operation window identification and energy consumption of the whole line. First, this study collects vibration, acoustic, and thermal signals from the bottle blowing, filling, and packaging sections; it also constructs cross-sectional anomaly characterization through time synchronization, feature-level alignment, and hierarchical fusion. Subsequently, Feather Convolutional Neural Network (FeatherCNN) is reconstructed using kernel fusion, channel compression, and 4-bit Integer (INT4) quantization to reduce model computation and storage load; thus, the network can adapt to resource-constrained Advanced RISC Machine (ARM) edge controllers. Finally, a dual-layer control chain is built, composed of continuous basic energy-saving and anomaly risk-weighted correction, so that anomaly scores influence the updates of temperature zones, valve openings, and heat-sealing parameters via dynamic weights and adjustment gains. The experimental results demonstrate that the anomaly window recognition accuracy of multimodal FeatherCNN reaches 0.931, which is superior to traditional machine learning models, deep learning baselines and various single-modal structures. The lightweight processing reduces Floating-Point Operations (FLOPs) from 3.42×10⁹ to 0.58×10⁹, a decrease of approximately 83%. The inference latency of the complete model on the ARM controller is shortened from 18.63 milliseconds (ms) to 7.41 ms. Under the controlled conditions of fixed production line speed, material specifications, and statistical windows, the dual-layer collaborative control has reduced the overall energy consumption of the whole line by 26%. The results show that multimodal anomaly identification, model lightweighting, and energy-saving parameter tuning can work together in the same edge decision chain. The framework verifies the feasibility of resource-constrained controllers supporting abnormal monitoring and energy consumption regulation of the entire packaging line; meanwhile, it provides an engineering reference for edge intelligent deployment of similar high-speed liquid packaging lines.

stories.title: Comparison of systemic inflammatory indices and periodontal parameters in patients with rheumatoid arthritis and gouty arthritis with periodontitis
stories.description: The aim of this study was to compare systemic inflammatory indices—including the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR)—and clinical periodontal parameters in systemically healthy patients with periodontitis and patients with periodontitis and concomitant rheumatoid arthritis (RA) or gouty arthritis (GA). 66 participants were divided into three groups: systemically healthy patients with periodontitis (SHP, n = 22), patients with RA and periodontitis (RAP, n = 22) and patients with GA and periodontitis (GAP, n = 22). Periodontal parameters and systemic inflammatory biomarkers SII, SIRI, AISI, NLR, PLR and MLR were assessed. The GAP group exhibited significantly lower probing pocket depth (PPD) and clinical attachment loss (CAL) values and neutrophil counts but higher lymphocyte counts than the other groups (p < 0.05). SII, SIRI, and NLR values were significantly lower in the GAP group compared to the SHP and RAP groups, while AISI and MLR were significantly lower in the GAP group compared to the SHP group (p < 0.05). SII and NLR were positively correlated with BOP, PPD, and CAL (p < 0.05). SII and NLR were positively associated with BOP, PPD, and CAL. However, these findings demonstrate associations rather than diagnostic or prognostic utility and should be confirmed in larger prospective studies.

stories.title: SpecLLM: LLM-based VNIR spectral interpretation
stories.description: Visible and near-infrared (VNIR) spectroscopy identifies materials from characteristic spectral bands, and spectroscopists interpret spectra by features such as peak positions and intensities. Recent machine-learning and foundation models for hyperspectral data are highly effective but return numerical outputs or latent representations rather than such feature-level descriptions. Meanwhile, LLM-based spectral approaches have mostly provided raw numerical sequences. We present a method for making spectroscopic data accessible to large language models (LLMs) through compact, feature-based representations. Instead of supplying full spectra as comma-separated values (CSV), JavaScript Object Notation (JSON), or extensible markup language (XML), the proposed approach extracts summary statistics and discriminative extrema. It serialises them as either natural language or structured JSON. We evaluate prototype-based substance classification in two complementary scenes from an open-access VNIR hyperspectral blood dataset. For the selected models, compact feature representations were substantially more effective than raw numerical encodings, but less effective than a Random Forest operating on raw spectra. The natural-language format provides a human-readable, inspectable serialisation of compact spectral evidence and reduces prompt length compared with full-spectrum encodings. We also compared natural language and JSON feature representations and found them broadly comparable.

stories.title: Persistent hypertension and left ventricular remodeling after stenting for coarctation of the aorta: a single-center cohort study
stories.description: Persistent hypertension (HTN) remains common after covered stent implantation for coarctation of the aorta (CoA). However, existing evidence is derived predominantly from surgical repair cohorts and cross-sectional echocardiography, leaving the individual trajectory of left ventricular (LV) remodeling after stenting poorly defined. We retrospectively studied 84 patients with complete persistent HTN status, and 75 patients with paired follow-up echocardiography for LV remodeling analyses. Multivariable logistic and linear regression were performed to identify factors associated with persistent HTN and follow-up LV mass index (LVMI) separately. Paired changes in LV hypertrophy (LVH) and LV geometry were assessed using McNemar and Stuart-Maxwell tests. Persistent HTN occurred in 46 of 84 patients (54.8%) at a median clinical follow-up of 9 years, and was associated with older age at repair and higher preoperative systolic blood pressure. Higher follow-up LVMI was associated with higher baseline LVMI, male sex and longer follow-up duration. At a median echocardiographic follow-up of 2 years, LVH prevalence decreased from 41.3–24.0%. This net decline masked bidirectional individual trajectories: 19 of 31 patients with baseline LVH (61.3%) no longer met LVH criteria, whereas 6 of 44 patients without baseline LVH (13.6%) developed new-onset LVH. Anatomical relief after CoA stenting therefore does not preclude ongoing myocardial burden, and patients developing new-onset LVH would not be identified by preoperative risk stratification alone. Serial echocardiographic assessment should complement long-term blood pressure surveillance, though these findings require validation in larger cohorts with standardized follow-up.

stories.title: DashGuard: spatio-temporal deep learning for dashcam-based road accident anticipation
stories.description: Road traffic accidents claim roughly 1.35 million lives each year, with delayed hazard perception rather than mechanical failure implicated in most collisions. Dashcam-based accident anticipation offers a low-cost complement to sensor-heavy ADAS, yet controlled comparisons across architectures remain rare. We present DashGuard, which trains and evaluates six spatio-temporal models a 3D CNN, CNN+LSTM, CNN+Transformer, and three two-stream variants (lightweight CNN, ResNet-18, and Transformer) on the Car Crash Dataset (1500 crash and 2000 normal videos) under a consistent, leak-free protocol. A video-level 70/15/15 split prevents clip-level contamination; four-level soft labels encode temporal distance to the accident frame; and a two-clip temporal consistency gate substantially cuts false-positive alerts. On the held-out test set, the Two-Stream Transformer achieves AUC = 0.981 and F1 = 0.870, with recall of 0.991. The lightweight 3D CNN (AUC = 0.949, $$\approx $$180 K parameters) is a viable option for edge hardware. A React/FastAPI web interface supports interactive evaluation. The results show that explicitly separating motion and appearance via two-stream attention gives the clearest gains over single-stream designs on this task.
